$comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for Salesforce flow-type resolution. A feature of automation-flow-coordinate: consumed by the flow-type-resolver reference (flow-type-resolver.md, next to this file) and by coordinate's recipes/resolve-type/resolve-type.md, recipes/author/author.md (Phase 2), shared/decision-tree.md (thin pointer) and elements/start/start.md. A flow type is a (processType x triggerType [x recordTriggerType, runInMode]) tuple; `specCategory` is the coarse label used in summaries/reports. The AUTHORITATIVE supported set is `supportedTuples` (a full enumeration of the (processType x triggerType x recordTriggerType) combinations Project Codey supports); `categories` are the coarse resolver view over it. `supportedTuples` is validated against the live org by eval/verify_supported_types.py (org-check only: every tuple's processType must be in the org's list-process-types and every triggerType in list-trigger-types for that processType; no-trigger is valid by absence). Covers the four audience/engagement trigger types (AutomationEvent, List, CampaignMember, RecordQuery), plus IndivRelatedRecord (Engagement/Journey), FormSubmissionEvent (a Marketing form submission; Flow Builder lists it under the Automation Event picker but persists it as its own trigger type), Segment, BroadcastNoTrigger and OnDemandNoTrigger (marketing flows), DataCloudDataChange (org-gated: a single Data Cloud DMO record change, provisioned only on a Data Cloud org) and EvaluationFlow, that this org's automation-flow-coordinate skill supports. Org-gated types (Data Cloud triggers) are modeled first-class in the top-level `orgGating` block: each is a named feature, and a `supportedTuples` entry references it by id via `orgGated: <featureId>` so eval/verify_supported_types.py and the resolver can detect provisioning from the org read endpoints and skip it as informational (surfacing a clean 'org not provisioned' outcome) on an org that lacks the feature, rather than failing.

axes.$comment: The characteristics of *what is being automated* that drive the process family. Combination is weighted / dominant-signal (NOT strict conjunction): lean toward Process when clearly multi-stage + long-running, even if one axis is ambiguous. Secondary factors (complexity, cognitive overload, manageability) are tie-breakers that promote a borderline Task->Process.
axes.processVsTask: Is it a single unit of work (Task) or a coordinated multi-stage business process (Process)?
axes.runningTime: Does it complete in one session/transaction (Short) or span time, wait for humans/events, and resume (Long)?
axes.collaboration: Does one actor do it (Single) or does it coordinate multiple users/teams/approvers across stages (Collaboration)?
axes.invocation: How does it START? Automatically on a record change (record-change), on a time schedule (scheduled), on a platform event (platform-event), on an email-engagement event such as open/click/bounce/response (automation-event), when someone submits a Marketing form (form-submission), or for a marketing/audience source — a Data Cloud segment (segment), an Actionable List (list), a Campaign's members (campaign-member), or all records of an object matching a filter (record-query) — VS. explicitly kicked off with no automatic trigger: launched by a person who steps through it (user-interactive) or called headlessly from Apex/API/a subflow/a button (on-demand). This is the axis that separates the Autolaunched families from their Record-Triggered / Scheduled / etc. counterparts: a record merely being *mentioned* as context is not a record trigger — only automatic firing on save is.

characteristicValues.$comment: Closed legal-value sets for each characteristics axis (the `axes` above are the human descriptions; these are the enumerable values a category may declare). Consumers reference these instead of hard-coding literals, and loadTaxonomy() validates every category's characteristics against them.

orgGating.$comment: First-class org-gating model. Some `supportedTuples` need a feature or provisioning the base org may lack; each such need is defined here ONCE as a named feature, and a tuple references it by id via `orgGated: <featureId>` (previously a bare tactical string, applied to DataCloudDataChange only). Consumers — eval/verify_supported_types.py and the flow-type-resolver reasoning — look the feature up to decide how to DETECT provisioning and what to tell the user when it is absent, instead of special-casing an individual trigger. `detectBy` names the org read-endpoint signal that reveals provisioning: `triggerType` (the gated trigger appears in list-trigger-types only when the feature is provisioned) or `processType` (the gated process type appears in list-process-types only when the feature is provisioned). `requires` is the human precondition; `minApiVersion`, where set, is the floor for the feature's metadata. `notProvisioned` is the clean, user-facing outcome the resolver surfaces (and the validator's skip note carries) when the org lacks the feature. Non-gated tuples (those without `orgGated`) are unaffected. This model generalizes: DataGraphDataChange, when its tuples are added, references the `data-cloud` feature (same Data Cloud provisioning, detectBy triggerType), and any future org-gated process type gets a `detectBy: processType` feature.

data-cloud.label: Data Cloud
data-cloud.notProvisioned: the org is not provisioned for Data Cloud (API version 59.0+); stop and tell the user rather than falling back to a core record trigger

supportedTuples.$comment: AUTHORITATIVE supported set: the full enumeration of (processType x triggerType x recordTriggerType) combinations Project Codey supports, curated to the subset the automation-flow-coordinate skill can author (narrower than the org's full capability). A no-trigger entry omits `triggerType` (it is valid by ABSENCE, not by a `None` trigger value in the org's list-trigger-types). `recordTriggerType` is enumerated per the skill's start-element pairing table; the org's read endpoints do not gate it (getFlowCapabilities returns 200 even for an invalid recordTriggerType), so it is advisory and enforced only at save-time. `runInMode`, where set, is validated against getFlowCapabilities.runInModes. Every processType/triggerType/recordTriggerType/runInMode value here MUST appear in the corresponding `enums` list; validated org-side by eval/verify_supported_types.py. An entry may also carry an advisory `uiLabel` — the finer Flow Builder picker name (e.g. 'Before Save'/'After Save'/'Before Delete', which all map to specCategory `RecordTriggered`); it is display metadata only, NOT an org-validated value, and the validator ignores it. An entry may also carry `orgGated` — the id of a feature defined in the top-level `orgGating.features` block (e.g. "data-cloud") — to mark a type that exists only on an org provisioned for that feature. eval/verify_supported_types.py resolves the feature and, per its `detectBy`, treats the tuple as skipped-informational when the org lacks the feature (its triggerType absent from list-trigger-types, or its processType absent from list-process-types) and validates it normally when the org exposes it; an `orgGated` value naming no defined feature is a config violation. See `orgGating` for the model.

unsupportedProcessTypes.$comment: Out-of-scope process types the resolver does NOT author but must recognize in order to hand off. INTENTIONALLY NOT part of `enums.processType` or `supportedTuples` — the org-validator (eval/verify_supported_types.py) must never iterate these (it would reject them as unsupported). This block is the single home for the process-type glossary formerly duplicated in automation-flow-coordinate's shared/flow-properties/flow-properties.md. `label` = Flow Builder picker name; `processType` = metadata API value; `note` = why out of scope plus any distinguishing build fact. Feature families that are not a single processType (e.g. CPQ) stay as SKILL.md prose, not entries here.

entries.label: Field Service Mobile
entries.note: Offline mobile scenarios. Out of scope — hand off.

entries.label: Field Service Web
entries.note: Field Service (web). Out of scope — hand off.

entries.label: Data Capture Flow
entries.note: Offline data collection; can be LLM-targetable (see automation-flow-coordinate shared/flow-properties/flow-properties.md). Out of scope — hand off.

entries.label: Unified Scheduling Flow
entries.note: Unified scheduling scenarios; supports the Screen Progress Indicator (see flow-properties.md). Out of scope — hand off.

categories.label: Autolaunched Flow
categories.$note: A marketing send (email, SMS, journey) that an app or the API starts for one person, or a request that names the On-Demand Flow type, is OnDemandNoTrigger, not this no-trigger type: a no-trigger flow's action catalog does not offer the E360 send actions (sendEmailMessage, sendSmsMessage, sendToJourney). The send action decides, not the launch channel: an email or text sent with consent from a communication subscription is a marketing send (sendEmailMessage / sendSmsMessage); emailAlert and emailSimple take no subscription. A core emailSimple, a subflow or an Apex/REST utility flow stays here, and so does a flow described only as running on demand (called from Apex, a button or another flow) with no marketing send.

categories.label: Automation Event-Triggered Flow
keywords: fires when an email is opened/clicked/bounced/responded to

categories.label: Form-Triggered Flow
categories.$note: A Marketing form (a Form Builder form stored as Managed Content, type sfdc_cms__form) is submitted; the flow runs headless on each submission and reads the submitted fields via $Form. Flow Builder lists Form Submission under the Automation Event picker, but selecting it persists the flow as triggerType FormSubmissionEvent, so FormSubmissionEvent is the canonical saved shape, NOT AutomationEvent. HARD PROHIBITION: never author a form-submission flow as triggerType AutomationEvent with eventName/eventType trgrOnFormSubmission (the platform rejects it; see badPairs). Distinct from a Screen flow, which IS a form a user steps through interactively. Per-trigger build detail lives in automation-flow-coordinate's elements/start/form-submission-triggered.md.

categories.label: Segment-Triggered Flow
categories.$note: A broadcast that fans out a dynamic segment now is BroadcastNoTrigger, not Segment. Segment is the scheduled or on-activate audience trigger and keeps the Individual-only eligibility gate.

categories.label: Broadcast Flow
categories.$note: Start fan-out, not a canvas action. actionType cdpJitSegment; actionName and nameSegment are the segment API name. isAsync false is Run Type Sync. No start.object and no schedule. Per-member fields are $Input.<segmentOnApiName>.<field>. The segment DMO may be Account or Unified Individual. Build detail is in elements/start/start.md.

categories.label: On-Demand Flow
keywords: marketing send triggered by the app for a person
categories.$note: A marketing flow an app or integration starts through the API for one person. Top-level dataSpace required. No start.object, filters or schedule. A send's recipient comes from the reserved request inputs IndividualId / EmailAddress / TelephoneNumber, not an action parameter. Optional dataGraph (primary DMO Unified Individual or Individual) exposes $SelectedIndividual. Output variables are not returned in the launch response. Can't be a subflow. An email or text sent with consent from a communication subscription is a marketing send (sendEmailMessage / sendSmsMessage), never emailAlert or emailSimple. "On demand" alone (runs when called from Apex, a button or another flow, with no marketing send) is Autolaunched, not this type. Build detail is in elements/start/start.md.

categories.label: List-Triggered Flow
keywords: run for each record in a list

categories.label: RecordQuery-Triggered Flow
keywords: all records of an object matching a filter

categories.label: Record-Triggered Orchestration
keywords: multi-stage process starting on a record change
orchestrate work when a record is created/updated
route the work across stages on save

categories.label: Autolaunched Orchestration
keywords: track the work that needs to be done
a user can kick off / start / initiate the process
started from a button or on demand (NOT automatically on record save)
launch the coordinated process when someone chooses to

categories.label: Record-Triggered Approval Orchestration
keywords: approval that starts when a record is created/updated
route for sign-off on record change

categories.label: Autolaunched Approval Orchestration
keywords: a user submits / sends the record for approval
kicked off when someone submits it (NOT automatically on record save)

categories.label: Engagement / Journey-Triggered Flow (Individual Related Record)
keywords: pauses mid-flow until an engagement event
wait for the customer to click
categories.$note: Also called a CRM Triggered Flow ('CRM Triggered', 'CRM Trigger'). Flow Builder lists it under Automation Event-Triggered Flow as 'Prospect, Lead, Contact or Related Record Change'. People also say it for a core Record-Triggered Flow, so the name alone does not decide. A request that names a CRM Triggered Flow AND says 'marketing' resolves here with no question, even when the rest of it uses record-change wording ('every time a Contact is updated'): that wording sets the Start object and recordTriggerType, not the trigger type. Without 'marketing', lean here but set mustAsk and ask: a marketing Automation Event flow (Prospect, Lead, Contact or Related Record Change), or a Record-Triggered Flow (RecordAfterSave, which rejects the marketing sendEmailMessage action with ACTIONCALL_NOT_SUPPORTED_FOR_PROCESSTYPE, so an email there uses the core Send Email action). Never the Data Cloud-triggered DataCloudDataChange (a Data Cloud DMO change). It needs no mid-flow wait to be this type. Per-trigger build detail (builderType JourneyBuilder, triggering record as $Input, required dataSpace) lives in automation-flow-coordinate's elements/start/start.md, Engagement / Journey-Triggered section.

categories.label: Data Cloud-Triggered Flow
keywords: when a data cloud dmo record changes
data model object created or updated
categories.$note: Org-gated: requires a Data Cloud-provisioned org (API version 59.0+). The single-DMO record-change trigger — fires on one `ssot__*__dlm` DMO create/update, exposes the changed DMO as read-only `$Record`; distinct from the multi-object `DataGraphDataChange`, from core-SObject record triggers, and from `AutomationEvent`. Per-trigger build detail lives in automation-flow-coordinate's elements/start/data-cloud-data-change-triggered.md.

categories.label: Evaluation Flow
keywords: flow that decides whether an orchestration step can start or a step or stage can finish
categories.$note: The determination flow behind an orchestration's entry/exit criteria: a restricted, read-only autolaunched flow (no record writes, actions, Apex, waits, or screens; subflows must also be EvaluationFlows) that returns the Boolean output `isOrchestrationConditionMet`. Normally co-generated or referenced from an Orchestrator / ApprovalWorkflow via elements/entry-exit-criteria/entry-exit-criteria.md, which carries the hand-off contract. Resolve here directly only on an explicit Evaluation Flow request; do not over-route generic automation to it. Next Best Action does NOT use EvaluationFlow — NBA recommendation logic is a RecommendationStrategy flow.

badPairs.implies: Before-save flow that sends email, makes a callout, or updates a related record
badPairs.why: Before-save cannot perform those operations and only mutates the triggering record in-place

badPairs.implies: Screen element inside an AutoLaunchedFlow or the background steps of an Orchestration
badPairs.why: Screen elements are not supported in headless contexts
badPairs.redesign: Net-new / GENERATE only: use processType Flow for a Screen Flow; model the interactive work as an interactive Orchestration stage; or split the work so a headless flow (AutoLaunchedFlow, or a platform event-triggered flow) does the background steps and a SEPARATE Screen Flow — launched by a user, not by the event — does the interactive part (see anti-patterns.md). In EVOLVE — editing a supplied flow — this pair is a process-type change: decline per recipes/author/author.md Phase 0; do not propose a separate flow.

badPairs.why: Wait elements are not allowed in before-save context
badPairs.redesign: Use RecordAfterSave, or move the wait into a subflow

badPairs.implies: Orchestrator or ApprovalWorkflow using RecordBeforeSave / RecordBeforeDelete
badPairs.why: Orchestrations run asynchronously across stages; they trigger only after the record is committed

badPairs.implies: Marketing campaign targeting an audience/segment but using Scheduled or RecordAfterSave
badPairs.why: Those triggers have no concept of segment/list/campaign membership, audience exclusion, or marketing frequency caps
badPairs.redesign: Use triggerType Segment, List, CampaignMember, or RecordQuery — whichever matches the audience source the user described. A broadcast that fans out a dynamic segment now is BroadcastNoTrigger, not Segment.

badPairs.implies: A 'fire when the email is opened/clicked/bounced/responded-to' flow built as a Segment/record flow + a Wait Until Event element — or vice-versa
badPairs.why: IndivRelatedRecord (or Segment) + WaitUntilEvent runs the flow first and PAUSES for the event; AutomationEvent FIRES the whole flow when the event occurs. They are not interchangeable.
badPairs.redesign: Fire-on-event -> triggerType AutomationEvent. Run-then-wait -> Segment/record trigger + a WaitUntilEvent element mid-flow.

badPairs.implies: A form-submission flow built as triggerType AutomationEvent with eventName/eventType trgrOnFormSubmission (the Form Submission row that event discovery returns when scoped to the Automation Event trigger)
badPairs.why: PROHIBITED. Flow Builder lists Form Submission under the Automation Event picker, but selecting it saves the flow as triggerType FormSubmissionEvent. The platform rejects AutomationEvent + trgrOnFormSubmission: the event name is invalid (rewritten to nullNotFound on save), the flow saves as InvalidDraft, and $Form references no longer resolve. Never emit it, even when the user says 'Automation Event' or discovery returns trgrOnFormSubmission.
badPairs.redesign: Use triggerType FormSubmissionEvent with start.form = the form's content FQN and read the submitted fields via $Form.<field> (see elements/start/form-submission-triggered.md).

badPairs.implies: A 'when someone submits our form' flow built as a Screen flow (processType Flow), or a form a user fills in step by step built as FormSubmissionEvent
badPairs.why: A submitted Marketing form fires a headless flow once per submission, with the answers in $Form; a Screen flow IS the form, stepped through interactively by a user. The word 'form' alone does not decide it.
badPairs.redesign: Submitted form (the flow reacts after someone submits it) -> triggerType FormSubmissionEvent. A form the user fills in or steps through inside the flow -> processType Flow (Screen).

badPairs.implies: A Data Cloud DMO (a `__dlm` object) record-change flow built as a core RecordAfterSave/RecordBeforeSave — or a core SObject trigger built as DataCloudDataChange
badPairs.why: DataCloudDataChange fires on a Data Cloud DMO record change and exposes the DMO as a read-only $Record; core record triggers fire on a CRM SObject. They are not interchangeable, and a DMO is never a writable DML target.
badPairs.redesign: A `__dlm` target -> triggerType DataCloudDataChange (single DMO) or DataGraphDataChange (data graph). A core SObject -> RecordAfterSave / RecordBeforeSave / RecordBeforeDelete.

badPairs.implies: A broadcast flow, or a flow that fans out a dynamic segment now, built as triggerType Segment
badPairs.why: Segment is a scheduled or on-activate audience trigger and rejects non-Individual segments. BroadcastNoTrigger fans the segment out from the start, including an Account segment, with no schedule.
badPairs.redesign: Use triggerType BroadcastNoTrigger. Put the segment on start.fanOutAction (actionType cdpJitSegment, actionName = the segment API name). Do not apply the Segment eligibility gate.

badPairs.implies: An On-Demand Flow, or a marketing send that an app or the API starts for one person, built as a no-trigger autolaunched flow
badPairs.why: A no-trigger AutoLaunchedFlow rejects marketing send actions (You can't use the Send SMS Message action type in flows with the Autolaunched Flow process type).
badPairs.redesign: Use triggerType OnDemandNoTrigger with a top-level dataSpace (resolved as in elements/start/audience-common.md, Set the data space). Take the recipient from the reserved request inputs; do not add a recipient parameter.
